title: Panzanella
subtitle: Tuscan tomato and bread salad with capers and olives
excerpt: Panzanella is a Tuscan salad built around very ripe tomatoes and stale bread. The bread soaks up the tomato juices and dressing and becomes wonderfully soft and flavoursome. It is best made an hour before serving so the flavours can meld.
sourceNotes: Panzanella has been made in Tuscany since at least the sixteenth century. It was originally a frugal way to use up stale bread, and tomatoes were added once they arrived in Italy from the Americas.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble up to 2 hours ahead and leave at room temperature. Do not refrigerate or the bread goes gluey.

content.text: Use the ripest tomatoes you can find. Tear about 200g of stale sourdough or ciabatta into rough chunks and let it sit in the dressing for at least an hour before serving. The bread should be fully saturated but not falling apart.
Tear about 200g of day-old or stale dense bread into rough 3cm chunks. Place in a large bowl.

Add the tomatoes to the bowl, including any juices from the chopping board. Season with a good pinch of salt and the red wine vinegar. Toss well and leave for 15 minutes so the bread starts absorbing the juices.
Add the cucumber, red onion, olives, capers and olive oil. Toss everything together and leave to rest for at least 45 minutes at room temperature.
Taste and adjust the seasoning. Scatter over the basil just before serving.

items.cause: Bread was too fresh or soaked too long.
items.fix: Use older, denser bread and serve within 2 hours.

items.cause: Tomatoes lacked flavour or not enough salt.
items.fix: Add more salt and a splash of extra vinegar.
